english: After the COLLECT (which may be found in its proper place) the following is the second Collect from Candlemas day to Passion Sunday, and from the III. Sunday after Pentecost till Advent, except on Doubles or within Octaves; the third is at the choice of the Priest, and may be found amongst the Occasional Prayers, page
notes: Opens with a printed pointing-hand ornament (manicule) which the English column itself does not reproduce as text. Set in italic with roman for the emphasised words; COLLECT is small capitals. IMPORTANT: printed page xx carries NO facing Latin column at all - the whole page is set to the full measure in English only - so latin_incipit is empty for every block on xx. The rubric ends with the bare word `page` and no number: the cross-reference was never set in type. Right-margin ink loss: `from` prints as `f.om` (the r has lost its arm) and `except` as `ex.ept` (the c has lost its bowl); both read at 1600 dpi and controlled against the parallel rubric on xxvii, which prints the same clause whole.

speaker: priest
english: II. COLLECT. A cunctis. Preserve us, O Lord, we beseech thee, from all dangers of body and soul: and by the intercession of glorious and blessed Mary, the ever Virgin Mother of God, of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, of blessed N. and of all the saints, grant us, in thy mercy, health, and peace that all adversities and errors being removed, thy Church may serve thee with a pure and undisturbed devotion. Through.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the 1962 Ordo prints no collect text at all, and the seasonal second-collect regime this block belongs to (Candlemas to Passion Sunday, III Sunday after Pentecost to Advent, except on Doubles and within Octaves) was abolished by the 1960 code of rubrics. The block carries its own printed label `II. COLLECT.` in roman capitals followed by the Latin incipit tag `A cunctis` in italic; the element key is taken from that tag, no facing Latin column being printed. The book sets NO comma after `peace`: the terminal e of `peace` is undamaged at 1600 dpi, so the omission is the printing's own and not scan loss. Conclusion abbreviated to `Through.`

english: From Low Sunday inclusively till the Ascension, instead of the foregoing, is said the COLLECT, Concede; with its corresponding Secret and P. Com. as in the Votive Mass, SALVE, of the B. V. M. page 507.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: a seasonal substitution rule for the second collect, which the 1962 Ordo does not carry. Italic with roman for the emphasised words; COLLECT in full capitals, SALVE in small capitals. `P. Com.` (Post Communion): the m has lost its right arch and prints as `Coni.`; read at 1600 dpi, where no i-dot stands over the last stroke, so the letter is a broken m.

english: After the Collect or Collects, the EPISTLE is read. At the end whereof the Assistants answer Deo gratias; then follows the GRADUAL or the TRACT, either of which may be seen in their proper places.
notes: Italic, turned over four lines to the full measure. EPISTLE, GRADUAL and TRACT are set in small capitals. `Deo gratias` is in roman. The book prints no text of Epistle, Gradual or Tract here.

english: The Prayer, Munda cor meum, before the Gospel.
notes: Italic, with the Latin incipit `Munda cor meum` in roman. It does the work of a heading but is set as an indented italic rubric line like the others on this page, so kind is rubric rather than heading.

speaker: priest
english: CLEANSE my heart and my lips, O Almighty God, who didst cleanse the lips of the prophet Isaiah with a burning coal: and vouchsafe, through thy gracious mercy, so to purify me, that I may worthily attend to thy holy Gospel. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: Two-line drop capital C, the following LEANSE in small capitals, transcribed here as ordinary capitals. `Amen` in italic. No Latin is printed for this prayer.

speaker: priest
english: May the Lord be in my heart, and on my lips, that I may worthily, and in a becoming manner attend to his holy Gospel. Amen.
notes: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: this printing gives the blessing formula `Dominus sit in corde meo` alone and omits the petition `Jube, Domine, benedicere` that precedes it in the Ordo Missae. The element key is taken from the received Latin incipit, which this page does not print. `Amen` in italic.

speaker: priest
english: P. The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. P. The continuation (or the beginning) of the holy Gospel according to, &c. R. Glory be to thee, O Lord.
notes: Facing Latin and English columns resume at the head of xxi. One printed block containing both P. and R.; speaker given as priest on the precedent of the Canon file. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: `holy` prints as `ho ly`, the l reduced to a fragment, and the final `&c.` has lost the bowl of its c; both read at 1600 dpi and controlled against the facing Latin `P. Sequentia (vel initium) sancti Evangelii secundum, &c.`

english: The Gospel may be seen in its proper place.
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Gospel` in roman. The book prints no Gospel text here.

english: At the end of the Gospel, the Assistants answer,
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Gospel` in roman.

speaker: server
english: R. Praise be to thee, O Christ.
notes: Set in the facing columns, the Latin occupying one line and the English two.

english: Then they say with the Priest, in a low voice,
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Priest` in roman. DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: there the words that follow are the priest's own, said silently while he kisses the book; here the assistants are directed to say them with him.

speaker: all
english: May our sins be blotted out by the words of the Gospel.
notes: Set to the full measure with no facing Latin. Speaker given as `all` because the book's own preceding rubric says the assistants say it with the Priest. The element key is taken from the received Latin incipit, which this page does not print.

english: The NICENE CREED.
notes: Centred across the full measure; `The` in ordinary upper and lower case, `NICENE CREED` in full capitals.

english: I Believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible.
notes: The book prints no speaker for the Creed, so speaker is left empty. Two-line drop capital in both columns: C with REDO in capitals in the Latin, I with `Believe` in ordinary upper and lower case in the English, so the English drop capital is followed by a capitalised `Believe`, which is transcribed as printed.

latin_incipit: Et in unum Dominum Jesum Christum
english: And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God, and born of the Father before all ages. God of God; Light of Light; true God of true God; begotten not made; consubstantial to the Father, by whom all things were made. Who for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven, and became incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: AND WAS MADE MAN.* He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And the third day he rose again according to the Scriptures. And ascended into heaven, sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And he is to come again with glory to judge both the living and the dead, of whose kingdom there shall be no end.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxi/xxii, breaking in the English at `the Virgin` / `Mary` and in the Latin at `ex Maria Vir-` / `gine`. AND WAS MADE MAN is set in full capitals, matching the Latin ET HOMO FACTUS EST in the facing column; the asterisk after MAN. is the book's own and keys the footnote at the foot of xxii (see nota-incarnationis). Right-margin ink loss at the foot of xxi: `Virgin` prints with a damaged n reading almost as `Virgio`; read at 640 and 1600 dpi against the facing Latin `ex Maria Virgine`. The English renders `consubstantialem Patri` as `consubstantial to the Father`, not `with the Father`.

english: And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father and the Son; who, together with the Father and the Son, is adored and glorified; who spoke by the prophets. And one holy Catholic and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. And I expect the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.
notes: The facing Latin prints `qui ex Patre Filioque procedit`, so this printing DOES carry the Filioque, and the English renders it `who proceedeth from the Father and the Son`. The facing Latin prints `Et expecto resurrectionem mortuorum`, with expecto and NOT exspecto; read at 640 dpi in the lat-bot crop, where the word stands whole and unbroken at `Et expecto` on its own line. `Amen` in italic. A stray inked dot stands between `prophetas.` and `Et unam` in the Latin column.

speaker: priest
english: P. The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit.
notes: Set in the facing columns immediately after the Creed. The `Oremus` that completes this greeting is carried over to the head of xxiii and is entered separately below.

english: * At these words the assistants kneel down to adore God for the ineffable mystery of the incarnation.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: a devotional footnote for the reader, not a rubric of the Ordo. Set in roman to the full measure at the foot of xxii, below the columns, keyed by the asterisk to AND WAS MADE MAN. in the Creed. Entered as kind rubric because the fixed vocabulary has no value for a footnote; it is a note, not a rubric of the rite.

speaker: priest
english: Let us pray.
notes: Italic in both columns, set as the first line of xxiii in the facing columns. No response is printed; it completes the greeting at the foot of xxii. Entered as kind dialogue for want of a closer value.

english: Here follows the OFFERTORY, which may be seen in its proper place.
notes: Italic across the full measure, turned over two lines; OFFERTORY in full capitals. The book prints no offertory antiphon text here.

english: OBLATION of the HOST.
notes: Centred across the full measure. OBLATION and HOST are in small capitals; `of the` is in italic upper and lower case.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens aeterne Deus
english: Accept, O holy Father, almighty and eternal God, this unspotted Host, which I thy unworthy servant offer unto thee, my living and true God, for my innumerable sins, offences, and negligences, and for all here present; as also for all faithful Christians, both living and dead; that it may avail both me and them unto life everlasting. Amen.
notes: `Amen` in italic. A stray inked dot stands between `negligences,` and `and` in the English column; the comma itself is clear at 1600 dpi, so the mark is dirt and not punctuation. No cross sign is printed in either column.

english: When the Priest puts the Wine and Water into the Chalice, he says,
notes: Italic across the full measure, turned over two lines, with `Priest`, `Wine`, `Water` and `Chalice` in a heavier italic. The book gives no blessing of the water and no `Deus qui humanae` cross sign.

speaker: priest
english: O God, who, in creating human nature, hast wonderfully dignified it, and still more wonderfully reformed it: grant that by the mystery of this Water and Wine, we may be made partakers of his divine nature, who vouchsafed to become partaker of our human nature, namely, Jesus Christ our Lord thy Son, who with thee, in the unity of, &c. Amen.
notes: `namely` and `Amen` in italic. The conclusion is abbreviated to `in the unity of, &c.` where the facing Latin sets it out in full to `per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.` Right-margin ink loss: `unity` prints as `unitj`, the y having lost its tail, and the closing `Amen.` is broken to `Anun.`; both read at 640 dpi against the facing Latin.

english: OBLATION of the CHALICE.
notes: Centred across the full measure. OBLATION and CHALICE in small capitals, `of the` in italic upper and lower case.

speaker: priest
english: We offer unto thee, O Lord, the chalice of salvation, beseeching thy clemency: that it may ascend before thy divine Majesty, as a sweet odour, for our salvation, and for that of the whole world. Amen.
notes: `Amen` in italic. The facing Latin prints `calicem, salutaris,` with a comma after calicem, which is the printing's own error for `calicem salutaris`.

english: When the Priest bows before the Altar, he says,
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: In spiritu humilitatis, et in animo
english: Accept us, O Lord, in the spirit of humility, and contrition of heart: and grant that the sacrifice we offer this day in thy sight, may be pleasing to thee, O Lord God.
notes: The book prints no Amen here, and the facing Latin ends at `Domine Deus.` The Latin sets `nodie` for `hodie`, the h having failed.

english: When he blesses the Bread and Wine, he says,
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Bread` and `Wine` in a heavier italic.

speaker: priest
english: Come, O almighty and eternal God, the sanctifier, and bless this sacrifice, prepared for the glory of thy holy name.
notes: No cross sign is printed in either column, where the Latin rite prescribes one at `benedic`. The book prints no Amen.

english: Here, in solemn Masses, he blesses the Incense, saying,
notes: A full-measure horizontal rule is printed across both columns immediately above this rubric, marking off the solemn-Mass incensation matter that follows; the rule is the only one of its kind in this range. Italic, with `Masses` and `Incense` in a heavier italic.

speaker: priest
english: May the Lord, by the intercession of blessed Michael the archangel, standing at the right hand of the Altar of Incense, and of all his elect, vouchsafe to bless this incense, and receive it as an odour of sweetness. Through, Amen.
notes: The English conclusion is abbreviated to `Through,` with a comma and then `Amen.` in italic, where the facing Latin sets `Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.` in full. Both `Through,` and `Amen.` are undamaged at 640 dpi, so the comma is the printing's own.

english: At incensing the Bread and Wine, he says,
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Bread` and `Wine` in a heavier italic.

speaker: priest
english: May this Incense which thou hast blest, O Lord ascend to thee, and may thy mercy descend upon us.
notes: `Incense` is capitalised in the English. The book prints no comma after `O Lord`; the line runs on within the measure, so this is not scan loss. No Amen.

english: At incensing the Altar, he says, Ps. cxl.
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Altar` in a heavier italic and the psalm citation `Ps. cxl.` in roman.

speaker: priest
english: Let my prayer O Lord, be directed as incense in thy sight: the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice. Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth: and a door of prudence around my lips; that my heart incline not to evil words to make excuses in sins.
notes: The book prints no comma after the first `prayer`, putting it after `O Lord` instead; both words stand well inside the measure and are undamaged. The Latin `Dirigatur ... vespertinum` and `Pone Domine ... in peccatis` are set as one paragraph, and the English follows.

english: On giving the Censer to the Deacon, he says,
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Censer` and `Deacon` in a heavier italic. A stray inked mark stands immediately before `Deacon` in both the whole-page and the column renderings; it is dirt, not punctuation.

speaker: priest
english: May the Lord enkindle within us the fire of his love, and the flame of everlasting charity.
notes: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE in presentation, not in substance: the prayer is in the 1962 Ordo, but this printing sets it to the FULL MEASURE with NO facing Latin at all, and drops the Amen. It is the only offertory prayer on xxiii-xxvi so treated. The element key is taken from the received Latin incipit, which the page does not print.

english: Washing his Hands, he says, Ps. xxv. 6.
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `Hands` in a heavier italic and the psalm citation `Ps. xxv. 6.` in roman.

speaker: priest
english: I will wash my hands among the innocent: and will compass thy altar, O Lord.
notes: The Lavabo psalm is set as a run of separate printed paragraphs, one per verse, in both columns; each is entered here as its own row, following the book's own paragraphing.

speaker: priest
english: That I may hear the voice of thy praise: and tell all thy wondrous works.
notes: Right-margin ink loss: `the` at the end of the first line prints with a broken e, reading almost as `tho`; read against the facing Latin `Ut audiam vocem laudis`.

speaker: priest
english: I have loved O Lord, the beauty of thy house, and the place where thy glory dwelleth.
notes: The book prints no comma after `loved`, following the Latin `Domine dilexi decorem`, which is also unpunctuated after `Domine`.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Ne perdas cum impiis animam meam
english: Take not away my soul, with the wicked; nor my life with bloody men.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxv/xxvi, breaking in the English at `with the wicked;` / `nor my life`. The signature `C` stands at the foot of xxv.

speaker: priest
english: In whose hands are iniquities: their right-hand is filled with gifts.
notes: `right-hand` is hyphenated as printed.

speaker: priest
english: But I have walked in my innocence: redeem me and have mercy on me.

speaker: priest
english: My foot hath stood in the direct way: in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

speaker: priest
english: Glory be to the Father &c.
notes: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the doxology is abbreviated to its first words and `&c.` in both columns, where the Ordo Missae sets it out in full. The book prints no comma after `Father`, and no `Sicut erat` clause.

english: Bowing before the middle of the Altar, he says,
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Altar` in a heavier italic.

speaker: priest
english: Receive O holy Trinity, this oblation which we make to thee in memory of the Passion, Resurrection, and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in honour of the blessed Mary ever a virgin, of blessed John Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints: that it may be available to their honour, and our salvation: and may they vouchsafe to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we celebrate on earth. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: Scan damage of the end-of-line hyphen kind the shared brief warns of: the English breaks `Re-` / `surrection` and the hyphen has been eaten, so the page as scanned reads `Passion, Re surrection`; the facing Latin breaks the same word at `Re-` / `surrectionis` with its hyphen intact, and controls the reading. `Amen` in italic. The English names `blessed Mary ever a virgin` and `blessed John Baptist`; the Latin conclusion is abbreviated to `Per eumdem, &c. Amen.` while the English sets it out as `Through the same Christ our Lord.`

english: Then turning himself towards the People, he says,
notes: Italic across the full measure, with `People` in a heavier italic. This is the first block on xxvii, a leaf that this project has not previously transcribed; the running head on it is PREFACES., not THE ORDINARY, and the signature `C 2` stands at its foot.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Orate Fratres: ut meum ac vestrum
english: Brethren, pray that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God the Father Almighty.
notes: Neither column prefixes this block with `P.`, though the response that follows is prefixed `R.` in both. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: `my` at the end of the first English line prints with a broken y; read against the facing Latin `ut meum ac vestrum sacrificium`.

speaker: server
latin_incipit: R. Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus
english: R. May the Lord receive the sacrifice from thy hands, to the praise and glory of his name to our benefit, and to that of all his holy Church.
notes: The book prints NO comma after `name`, where the facing Latin has one after `nominis sui`; the terminal e of `name` is undamaged at 640 dpi, so the omission is the printing's own. The `R.` is printed in both columns and is kept in the English as the shared brief directs.

english: After reading the SECRET, which may be seen in its proper place, the second Secret from Candlemas-day, till Passion-Sunday and from the III. Sunday after Pentecost until Advent, (except on Doubles and within Octaves) is the following.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the seasonal second-Secret regime, matching the second-Collect rubric on xx. Italic across the full measure with roman for the emphasised words; SECRET in small capitals. `Candlemas-day` falls at a line break, so it cannot be settled whether the hyphen is the compound's own or the break's; the same book prints `Candlemas day` unhyphenated on xx. The opening parenthesis before `except` is printed without a closing space and the parenthesis is closed after `Octaves`.

speaker: priest
english: II. SECRET.—Graciously hear us, O God our Saviour; that by virtue of this sacrament, thou mayest defend us from all enemies, of both soul and body: grant us grace in this life, and glory in the next.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: a proper Secret printed bodily inside the Ordinary, the counterpart of the II. COLLECT on xx. Set to the FULL MEASURE with no facing Latin, so latin_incipit is empty. The label `II. SECRET.` is in roman capitals and is followed by an em rule, not a full stop and space. The element key is numbered from the printed label because the page prints no Latin incipit to derive one from. No conclusion is printed.

english: From Low-Sunday, exclusively, till the Ascension, instead of the foregoing is said the SECRET, * May, O Lord, &c, as in the Votive Mass, SALVE, of the B. V. M. p. 508.
notes: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the seasonal substitution rule for the second Secret. Italic with roman for the emphasised words; SECRET and SALVE in full capitals. The asterisk before `May` is printed on the page and has NO answering footnote anywhere on xxvii - the foot of the page carries only the signature `C 2` - so it stands unexplained. The book prints `&c,` with a comma, not `&c.` Note also `Low-Sunday, exclusively` here against `Low Sunday inclusively` in the matching collect rubric on xx.

speaker: priest
english: P. World without end. R. Amen.
notes: Set in the facing columns; the Latin runs over two lines, `P. Per omnia saecula.` then `saeculorum. R. Amen.`, the full stop after `saecula` being the printing's own error. `Amen` in italic in both columns.

english: The Preface.
notes: Centred in italic across the measure, above the dialogue. The common Preface itself begins on the following page and is outside this file.

speaker: priest
english: P. The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. P. Lift up your hearts. R. We have lifted them up to the Lord. P. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. R. It is meet and just.
notes: The whole Preface dialogue is set as one continuous block in each column, with the P. and R. run in. Scan damage of the end-of-line hyphen kind: the English breaks `lift-` / `ed` and the hyphen has been eaten, so the page as scanned reads `We have lift ed them up`; read against the facing Latin `R. Habemus ad Dominum.` and against the book's own unbroken usage. This is the last block on xxvii; `C 2` stands beneath it.
